It passes directly through the obturator canal
It exits through the obturator foramen and enters the deep perineal pouch
It passes through the inguinal canal
questions.explain: The pudendal nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, hooks around the sacrospinous ligament near the ischial spine, and enters the perineum through the lesser sciatic foramen.

open.q: Name the structure or anatomical relationship tested in this clinical scenario.
accept: it exits the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen and re-enters through the lesser sciatic foramen

questions.q: Which anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic inlet is the shortest and is the critical one for passage of the fetal head?
questions.explain: The obstetric conjugate runs from the sacral promontory to the nearest point on the back of the pubic symphysis. The true conjugate ends on the upper border of the symphysis and is slightly longer.

open.q: What is the name of the shortest anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic inlet, which is critical for the fetal head?
accept: shortest AP diameter of the inlet
minimum AP diameter of the pelvic inlet

questions.q: Which pelvic diameter runs from the sacral promontory to the inferior border of the pubic symphysis and is measured on vaginal examination?
questions.explain: The diagonal conjugate is measured with the examining fingers. The obstetric conjugate is estimated by subtracting about 1.5 to 2 cm from it.

open.q: Which pelvic diameter, from the sacral promontory to the inferior border of the pubic symphysis, is measured clinically on vaginal examination?

questions.q: Which feature is typical of the female pelvis compared with the male pelvis?
questions.explain: The female pelvis has a wide subpubic angle, a round or oval inlet and a shallow, wide cavity. The other three features describe the male pelvis.

open.q: What is the typical subpubic (pubic arch) angle of the female pelvis compared with the male?

questions.q: Pelvic fractures most commonly injure which pair of structures?
questions.explain: The bladder and urethra lie directly behind the pubic bones and are torn by displaced fragments. Urethral rupture is especially common in males.

open.q: Which pelvic organs are most commonly injured in pelvic fractures?

questions.q: Which hormone mainly softens the pelvic ligaments and increases joint mobility in late pregnancy?
questions.explain: Relaxin, with progesterone, loosens the pelvic ligaments and the symphysis pubis. Oxytocin acts on uterine muscle and prolactin on the breast.

open.q: Which hormone softens the pelvic ligaments and joints in late pregnancy?
accept: relaxin from the corpus luteum and placenta

questions.q: Spondylolysis is a defect in which part of a lumbar vertebra?
questions.explain: Spondylolysis is a break in the pars interarticularis, the segment of the arch between the superior and inferior articular processes. L5 is the most common level.

open.q: Spondylolysis is a defect in which part of a lumbar vertebra?

questions.q: What is spondylolisthesis?
options: Fusion of L5 with the sacrum
Forward slip of L5 on S1
Collapse of a lumbar vertebral body
questions.explain: In spondylolisthesis a vertebra, most often L5, slips forward on the one below. Fusion of L5 with the sacrum is called sacralisation.

open.q: What is spondylolisthesis?
accept: forward slipping of one vertebra on another
anterior displacement of L5 on S1

questions.q: Which muscle forms the greater part of the pelvic diaphragm and is most often injured during childbirth?
questions.explain: Levator ani forms most of the pelvic floor. Its stretching or tearing in childbirth contributes to prolapse and incontinence. Coccygeus is a small posterior part of the diaphragm.

open.q: Which muscle forms the greater part of the pelvic diaphragm?

questions.q: Which spinal segments mainly supply levator ani through the nerve to levator ani?
questions.explain: The nerve to levator ani arises from S3 and S4, with a contribution from the perineal branch of the pudendal nerve.

open.q: Which spinal segments mainly supply levator ani?

questions.q: A woman develops flank pain and hydronephrosis after a hysterectomy in which the uterine artery was clamped close to the cervix. Which structure was most likely injured?
questions.explain: The ureter passes beneath the uterine artery about 2 cm lateral to the cervix, so it is easily clamped or tied by mistake.

open.q: A woman develops flank pain and hydronephrosis after a hysterectomy in which the uterine artery was clamped close to the cervix. Which structure was most likely injured?

questions.q: From which vessel does the ovarian artery arise?
questions.explain: The ovarian arteries arise from the abdominal aorta just below the renal arteries and descend in the suspensory ligament of the ovary.

open.q: From which vessel does the ovarian artery arise?
accept: abdominal aorta below the renal arteries

questions.q: After a radical prostatectomy a man cannot achieve an erection, although penile skin sensation is normal. Which nerves were most likely damaged?
questions.explain: The cavernous nerves carry parasympathetic fibres from S2-S4 that dilate the arteries of the erectile tissue. They run along the prostate and are vulnerable in its removal.

open.q: After a radical prostatectomy a man cannot achieve an erection, although penile skin sensation is normal. Which nerves were most likely damaged?

questions.q: Why can extensive stripping of the ureter during surgery lead to ureteric necrosis?
options: Adventitial vessels carry its segmental blood supply
Its only supply is a single renal trunk
Its supply comes from the superior vesical artery alone
Its supply depends on the testicular artery alone
questions.explain: The ureter is supplied by branches of the renal, gonadal, common iliac, internal iliac and vesical arteries, which run along its adventitia. Stripping this layer cuts off the blood supply.

open.q: Why can extensive stripping of the ureter during surgery lead to ureteric necrosis?
accept: segmental blood supply in the adventitia
blood supply runs along its outer sheath
several small arteries supply it from the side

questions.q: Which is the narrowest part of the ureter?
questions.explain: The ureterovesical junction, where the ureter passes obliquely through the bladder wall, is the narrowest part and is the commonest site of stone impaction.

open.q: Which is the narrowest part of the ureter, where calculi commonly lodge?
accept: where the ureter enters the bladder

questions.q: What is a cystocele?
options: Rectal herniation into the posterior vaginal wall
Bladder herniation into the anterior vaginal wall
questions.explain: A cystocele is herniation of the bladder into the anterior vaginal wall from weakness of the pelvic floor. The posterior equivalent is a rectocele.

open.q: What is a cystocele?
accept: bladder herniation into the anterior vaginal wall

questions.q: Stress urinary incontinence in women who have had several vaginal deliveries is mainly due to which problem?
questions.explain: Weak levator ani and endopelvic fascia no longer support the urethra and bladder neck, so urine leaks when intra-abdominal pressure rises. Overactive detrusor causes urge incontinence.

open.q: Stress urinary incontinence after childbirth is mainly due to weakness of which supporting structures?
accept: urethral support from the pelvic floor

questions.q: Why can a distended bladder be punctured just above the pubic symphysis without entering the peritoneal cavity?
options: Peritoneum is pushed upward as the bladder fills
The bladder lies within the peritoneal cavity when full
The bladder wall is fused with the rectus sheath
The retropubic space is filled with peritoneal fluid
questions.explain: As the bladder fills it rises above the pubis and strips the peritoneum off the lower anterior abdominal wall. A suprapubic needle then enters it extraperitoneally.

open.q: Why can a distended bladder be punctured just superior to the pubic symphysis without entering the peritoneal cavity?
accept: the peritoneum is lifted up by the full bladder
the bladder rises above the pubis and displaces peritoneum

questions.q: Intraperitoneal rupture of the urinary bladder usually involves which part?
questions.explain: Only the superior surface is covered by peritoneum, so a tear there leaks urine into the peritoneal cavity. Tears of the anteroinferior wall leak into the extraperitoneal retropubic space.

open.q: Which part of the urinary bladder ruptures into the peritoneal cavity?

questions.q: Which anatomical feature predisposes women to ascending urinary tract infection?
questions.explain: The female urethra is only about 4 cm long, so organisms from the perineum reach the bladder easily. The male urethra is about 18 to 20 cm long.

open.q: Which anatomical feature of the female urethra predisposes women to ascending urinary infection?
accept: short length of the female urethra

questions.q: Which structure can be palpated through the anterior rectal wall on digital rectal examination in a man?
questions.explain: The posterior surface of the prostate lies against the anterior rectal wall and can be assessed for size, consistency and nodules. Normal seminal glands are usually not palpable.

open.q: Which male gland is palpated through the anterior rectal wall on digital rectal examination?

questions.q: Which male accessory gland secretes a fructose-rich fluid that nourishes sperm?
questions.explain: The seminal glands (vesicles) provide most of the volume of semen, and their secretion is rich in fructose. The prostate secretes citrate and PSA.

open.q: Which male accessory gland secretes the fructose-rich fluid that nourishes sperm?

questions.q: Which structure is cut and ligated in a vasectomy?
questions.explain: The ductus deferens is divided through a small scrotal incision. Sperm cannot reach the urethra, but testosterone production is unaffected.

open.q: Which structure is cut and ligated in a vasectomy?

questions.q: In which zone of the prostate does benign prostatic hypertrophy mainly develop?
questions.explain: BPH arises in the transition zone around the prostatic urethra and compresses it, causing obstruction. Carcinoma arises mainly in the peripheral zone.

open.q: In which zone of the prostate does benign prostatic hypertrophy mainly develop?

questions.q: Prostatic cancer often spreads to the vertebrae and pelvic bones through which venous route?
questions.explain: The prostatic venous plexus communicates with the valveless internal vertebral venous plexus, so cancer cells can reach the vertebrae directly.

open.q: Through which venous route does prostatic cancer commonly spread to the vertebrae?

questions.q: Which investigation uses contrast injected through the cervix to assess patency of the uterine tubes?
questions.explain: In hysterosalpingography, contrast outlines the uterine cavity and tubes. Spill into the peritoneal cavity shows that the tubes are patent.

open.q: Which radiological investigation uses contrast injected through the cervix to assess patency of the uterine tubes?

questions.q: In which part of the uterine tube does an ectopic pregnancy most commonly occur?
questions.explain: Most tubal pregnancies implant in the ampulla, the widest part of the tube. Isthmic pregnancies are less common and rupture earlier.

open.q: In which part of the uterine tube does an ectopic pregnancy most commonly occur?

questions.q: Which structures are ligated or occluded in female tubal sterilisation?
questions.explain: The uterine tubes are tied, clipped or cut, which stops sperm from reaching the ovum. Ovulation and menstruation continue.

open.q: Which structures are ligated or occluded in female tubal sterilisation?

questions.q: A bicornuate uterus results from incomplete fusion of which embryonic structures?
questions.explain: The uterus and uterine tubes develop from the paramesonephric (Mullerian) ducts. Incomplete fusion of their lower parts gives a double or bicornuate uterus.

open.q: A bicornuate uterus results from incomplete fusion of which embryonic ducts?

questions.q: What is the normal position of the uterus?
questions.explain: In most women the cervix tilts forward on the vagina (anteversion) and the body bends forward on the cervix (anteflexion), so the uterus lies over the bladder.

open.q: What is the normal position of the uterus?

questions.q: A Pap smear for cervical cancer screening samples cells from which site?
questions.explain: The transformation zone at the squamocolumnar junction is where dysplasia and carcinoma usually begin. Cells are collected here with a spatula and brush.

open.q: From which site of the cervix are cells collected in a Pap smear?

questions.q: In culdocentesis, a needle is passed into which space and by which route?
options: Anterior fornix into the vesicouterine pouch
Lateral fornix into the broad ligament
Posterior fornix into the rectouterine pouch
questions.explain: The rectouterine pouch (pouch of Douglas) is the lowest part of the peritoneal cavity in women and lies behind the posterior fornix. Blood from a ruptured ectopic pregnancy collects there.

open.q: In culdocentesis, a needle is passed through which part of the vagina into the rectouterine pouch?
accept: posterior vaginal wall into the pouch of Douglas

questions.q: Pain of uterine contractions in the first stage of labour is carried by afferent fibres to which spinal segments?
questions.explain: Pain from the uterine body travels with sympathetic nerves to T10-L1. Pain from the cervix, vagina and perineum in the second stage travels to S2-S4 through the pudendal nerve.

open.q: Pain of uterine contractions in the first stage of labour is carried by afferent fibres to which spinal segments?
accept: lower thoracic and upper lumbar segments

questions.q: A mediolateral episiotomy is preferred in many centres because it reduces the risk of extension into which structure?
questions.explain: A midline tear can extend through the perineal body into the anal sphincter. A mediolateral cut runs away from the anus and lowers this risk.

open.q: A mediolateral episiotomy is preferred in many centres because it reduces the risk of tearing into which structure?

questions.q: A man falls astride a bar and develops perineal swelling. Urine extravasates into the scrotum, penis and lower abdominal wall but not into the thigh. Which structure is ruptured?
questions.explain: Rupture of the bulbar spongy urethra below the perineal membrane lets urine into the superficial perineal pouch. Colles fascia limits spread to the perineum, scrotum, penis and lower abdominal wall.

open.q: A man falls astride a bar and develops perineal swelling. Urine extravasates into the scrotum, penis and lower abdominal wall but not into the thigh. Which structure is ruptured?

questions.q: Internal haemorrhoids are painless because the anal canal above the pectinate line has which nerve supply?
questions.explain: Above the pectinate line sensation is carried by visceral afferents, which are insensitive to cutting and pinching. Below the line the somatic inferior rectal nerves make lesions painful.

open.q: Internal haemorrhoids are painless because the anal canal superior to the pectinate line has what type of nerve supply?

questions.q: Which vein mainly drains the anal canal above the pectinate line?
questions.explain: The superior rectal vein drains to the inferior mesenteric vein and the portal system. Below the line the inferior rectal veins drain systemically, so the pectinate line is a portosystemic anastomosis.

open.q: Which vein mainly drains the anal canal superior to the pectinate line?

questions.q: Anal fissures most commonly occur in which position?
questions.explain: The posterior midline is the least well supported part of the anal canal, so it tears most easily on passing hard stools. Fissures away from the midline suggest another disease such as Crohn disease.

open.q: In which position do anal fissures most commonly occur?
accept: posterior midline of the anal canal

questions.q: An ischio-anal abscess can spread to the opposite ischio-anal fossa through which route?
questions.explain: The two ischio-anal fossae communicate behind the anal canal, below the anococcygeal body. A horseshoe abscess spreads across this space.

open.q: An ischio-anal abscess can spread to the opposite ischio-anal fossa behind the anal canal. What is this route called?

questions.q: Which part of levator ani forms a sling behind the anorectal junction and maintains the anorectal angle for faecal continence?
questions.explain: Puborectalis pulls the anorectal junction forward, forming the anorectal angle that helps prevent faecal leakage.

open.q: Which part of levator ani forms a sling behind the anorectal junction and maintains faecal continence?

questions.q: Excluding the external urethral meatus, which part of the male urethra is the narrowest?
questions.explain: The membranous urethra passes through the deep perineal pouch, surrounded by the external urethral sphincter. It is the narrowest part apart from the meatus and is at risk during catheterisation.

open.q: Excluding the external urethral orifice, which part of the male urethra is the narrowest?
accept: part within the deep perineal pouch

questions.q: In hypospadias, where does the urethra open abnormally?
questions.explain: Hypospadias results from incomplete fusion of the urogenital folds, so the urethra opens on the underside of the penis. Opening on the dorsal surface is epispadias.

open.q: In hypospadias, where does the urethra open abnormally?
accept: on the lower surface of the penis

questions.q: What is phimosis?
options: Tight foreskin that will not retract
Retracted foreskin that will not return
Foreskin fused to the whole shaft
questions.explain: In phimosis the prepuce is too tight to be drawn back over the glans. Circumcision is a common treatment. A retracted foreskin that will not return is paraphimosis.

open.q: What is phimosis?
accept: tight foreskin that cannot be retracted

questions.q: What is paraphimosis?
options: Tight foreskin that cannot be retracted at all
Retracted foreskin trapped behind the glans
Foreskin fused to the glans by adhesions
Swelling of the shaft from lymphatic block
questions.explain: A retracted foreskin that is not brought forward again forms a tight band behind the glans. This impairs venous return and can threaten the glans, so it needs urgent reduction.

open.q: What is paraphimosis?
accept: retracted foreskin that cannot be returned over the glans
foreskin stuck behind the glans causing swelling
constricting ring of prepuce behind the glans

questions.q: Which nerve is blocked to anaesthetise the penile skin for circumcision?
questions.explain: The dorsal nerve of the penis is a branch of the pudendal nerve and supplies the skin of the penis, including the glans and prepuce.

open.q: Which nerve is blocked to anaesthetise the penile skin for circumcision?
accept: branch of the pudendal nerve to the penis

questions.q: Which mediator directly relaxes the smooth muscle of the corpora cavernosa to cause erection?
questions.explain: Nitric oxide raises cGMP and relaxes the cavernosal and helicine artery smooth muscle so the erectile tissue fills with blood. Sildenafil prolongs this effect by blocking cGMP breakdown.

open.q: Which gaseous mediator relaxes the smooth muscle of the corpora cavernosa to cause erection?

questions.q: Which muscle in the scrotal wall wrinkles the scrotal skin?
questions.explain: The dartos is smooth muscle in the scrotal wall that wrinkles the skin in the cold to reduce heat loss. Cremaster raises the testis.

open.q: Which smooth muscle in the scrotal wall wrinkles the scrotal skin?

questions.q: Cancer of the testis first spreads to which group of lymph nodes?
questions.explain: The testis develops near the kidney, so its lymph follows the testicular vessels to the para-aortic nodes at about L2. Scrotal skin drains to the superficial inguinal nodes.

open.q: Cancer of the testis first spreads to which group of lymph nodes?

questions.q: Where do the ducts of the greater vestibular glands open?
questions.explain: The greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands lie behind the bulbs of the vestibule and open into the vestibule beside the hymen. A blocked duct can form a cyst or abscess.

open.q: Where do the ducts of the greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands open?
accept: groove between the labium minus and the hymen

questions.q: In which canal does the pudendal nerve run along the lateral wall of the ischio-anal fossa?
questions.explain: The pudendal canal (Alcock canal) is a fascial sheath of obturator internus. It carries the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels into the perineum.

open.q: In which canal on the lateral wall of the ischio-anal fossa does the pudendal nerve run?

questions.q: Vaginismus is an involuntary spasm of which pelvic floor muscle?
questions.explain: In vaginismus the pelvic floor muscles around the vaginal opening, mainly levator ani, contract involuntarily, making penetration painful or impossible.

open.q: Vaginismus is an involuntary spasm of which pelvic floor muscle group?

questions.sub: Urinary bladder and pelvic autonomic nerves
questions.q: A man sustains a sacral nerve-root injury involving S2–S4. Which bladder function is most directly impaired by interruption of the pelvic splanchnic nerves?
options: Contraction of the detrusor muscle during micturition
Voluntary contraction of the external urethral sphincter
Sympathetic relaxation of the detrusor during storage
Somatic sensation from the skin of the perineum
questions.explain: Pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2–S4) carry parasympathetic fibres to the bladder. They promote detrusor contraction and facilitate voiding. The external urethral sphincter is supplied somatically by the pudendal nerve, while sympathetic pathways via the hypogastric plexus support urine storage.

questions.q: During pelvic surgery, the surgeon identifies the ureter near the posterolateral aspect of the urinary bladder. Which structure normally crosses superior to the ureter close to the bladder?
questions.explain: In the male pelvis, the ductus deferens crosses superior to the ureter near the posterolateral bladder before reaching the seminal gland and ejaculatory duct. This relationship is the male counterpart of the uterine artery crossing over the ureter in the female pelvis.
